units.title: Module 1: Introduction to Internet & Web Design
units.description: Basics of the Internet, websites, web technologies, website types, and web editors.

modules.title: Internet & Web Fundamentals
modules.description: What the Internet and the WWW are, and the key terms behind every website.

cards.title: Introduction to Internet
cards.body: The Internet is a worldwide network that connects computers and devices. It enables communication, information sharing and services such as email, online banking, education and e-commerce.

cards.title: WWW & Its Applications
cards.body: The World Wide Web (WWW) is a collection of interconnected web pages accessed through the Internet. The Internet is used for web browsing, communication, education, shopping, banking, entertainment and many other services. Note: the Internet is the network itself, while the WWW is one service that runs on top of it.

quiz.question: What does WWW stand for?
quiz.explanation: WWW stands for World Wide Web: the collection of interconnected web pages accessed through the Internet.

cards.title: Website, Webpage & URL
cards.body: A website is a collection of related web pages. A webpage is an individual page displayed in a browser. A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address used to locate a webpage or other web resource, e.g. https://www.example.com/index.html.

cards.title: IP Address & Browser
cards.body: An IP Address identifies a device on a network and enables communication between devices. A web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari) is software used to access and display websites.

quiz.question: What is a URL used for?
quiz.explanation: A URL is the address that locates a specific web resource, such as a webpage, on the Internet.

modules.title: Working of Websites
modules.description: How a request travels from the browser to the server, and the front end / back end split.

cards.title: Working of Websites
cards.body: When a user enters a URL, the browser sends a request to a web server. The server processes the request and sends the required resources back to the browser, which displays the webpage.

cards.title: Client & Server
cards.body: The client is usually the user's device or browser that requests information. The server receives the request and provides the required webpage, data or service.

quiz.question: Who receives a request from the browser and provides the required resources?
quiz.explanation: The server receives the client's request and responds with the webpage, data or service.

cards.title: Front End & Back End
cards.body: The Front End is the visible and interactive part of a website. The Back End works behind the scenes and handles processing, data and application logic.

cards.title: Client & Server-Side Scripting
cards.body: Client-side scripting runs mainly in the user's browser, while server-side scripting runs on the server to handle processing and data-related operations.

quiz.question: Which part of a website is directly visible to the user?
quiz.explanation: The Front End is everything the user sees and interacts with; the Back End works behind the scenes.

modules.title: Responsive & Types of Websites
modules.description: Designing for every screen, and the difference between static and dynamic sites.

cards.title: Responsive Web Design
cards.body: Responsive Web Design allows a website to adapt its layout and content to different screen sizes. It helps websites work effectively on mobiles, tablets, laptops and desktops.

cards.title: Why Responsive Matters
cards.body: A single responsive site replaces separate mobile and desktop versions. It improves user experience on any device and is achieved with flexible layouts, flexible images and CSS media queries, which you will learn in the CSS module.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of responsive web design?
options: To adapt webpages to different screen sizes
quiz.explanation: Responsive design makes one website adjust its layout and content to fit mobiles, tablets, laptops and desktops.

cards.title: Static Websites
cards.body: A static website mainly contains fixed content. The content generally remains the same and changes usually require the website files to be manually edited.

cards.title: Dynamic Websites
cards.body: A dynamic website can generate or update content based on users, data or server-side processing. It is commonly used for interactive websites and online applications.

quiz.question: Which type of website can generate changing content?
quiz.explanation: Dynamic websites generate or update content based on users, data or server-side processing.

modules.title: Web Editors
modules.description: Choosing a code editor and creating, saving and opening your first web files.

cards.title: Web Editors
cards.body: A code editor is used to create and modify source code. Notepad++, Sublime Text and Visual Studio Code are commonly used editors for web development.

cards.title: Using Editors
cards.body: Web editors provide features for writing, editing and managing web files. They make it easier to create and modify HTML and other web development files.

quiz.question: Which of the following is a code editor?
quiz.explanation: Notepad++ is a code editor used for writing HTML and other source code; the others are not.

cards.title: Creating & Editing Files
cards.body: Web editors allow users to create, write and modify web files. Common file types include HTML (.html), CSS (.css) and JavaScript (.js).

cards.title: Saving Files
cards.body: After creating or editing a file, it should be saved with the correct file extension. HTML files can be opened in a browser to view the webpage.

quiz.question: Which extension is commonly used for an HTML file?
quiz.explanation: HTML files are saved with the .html extension so the browser can open and render them.

modules.title: HTML Introduction & Basic Structure
modules.description: What HTML is, tags, elements, attributes, versions, DOCTYPE and the head section.

cards.title: HTML: A Markup Language
cards.body: HTML provides a way of displaying web pages with text and images or multimedia content. HTML is not a programming language, but a markup language. An HTML file is a text file containing small markup tags. The markup tags tell the web browser, such as Mozilla Firefox or Google Chrome, how to display the page.

cards.title: File Extension & Full Form
cards.body: An HTML file must have an .htm or .html file extension. HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.

quiz.question: What does HTML stand for?
quiz.explanation: HTML = HyperText Markup Language. It is a markup language, not a programming language.

cards.title: Static Pages
cards.body: Static pages, as the name indicates, comprise static content (text or images). So you can only see the contents of a web page without being able to have any interaction with it.

cards.title: Dynamic Pages
cards.body: Dynamic pages are those where the content of the web page depends on user input, so interaction with the user is required to display the page. Example: a web page asks for a number to find out if it is even or odd. When the user enters the number and clicks the button, the number is sent to the web server, which returns the result to the user in an HTML page.

quiz.question: Which page type needs user input to decide what content it shows?
quiz.explanation: Dynamic pages depend on user input (e.g. the even/odd number example); static pages only display fixed content.

cards.title: Container Tag
cards.body: A container tag has an opening and a closing tag. Examples: <html> ....... </html>, <head> ....... </head>, <body> ....... </body>.

cards.title: Name and Value
cards.body:
Attributes provide additional information about the contents of an element. They appear on the opening tag of the element and are made up of two parts: a name and a value, separated by an equals sign. Example:

Paragraph in English

cards.title: Attribute Rules (Part 1)
cards.body: The attribute name indicates what kind of extra information you are supplying about the element's content. It should be written in lowercase. The value is the information or setting for the attribute and should be placed in double quotes.

cards.title: Attribute Rules (Part 2)
cards.body: In the example, the lang attribute indicates the language used in the element; its value specifies US English. Note: HTML5 allows uppercase attribute names and omitting the quote marks, but this is not recommended.

quiz.question: How should attribute values be written?
quiz.explanation: Values go in double quotes and attribute names in lowercase. HTML5 tolerates otherwise, but it is not recommended.

cards.title: HTML Tag
cards.body: <HTML> is a starting tag. To delimit the text inside, add a closing tag by adding a forward slash "/" to the starting tag. Most but not all tags have a closing tag. The code for an HTML page is written between <HTML> and </HTML>. <HTML> tells the browser 'this is the start of an HTML document' and </HTML> 'this is the end of an HTML document'.

cards.title: Head Tag
cards.body: Before the <body> element you will often see a <head> element. It contains information about the page, rather than information shown within the main part of the browser. You will usually find a <title> element inside <head>.

cards.title: Title Tag
cards.body: The contents of the <title> element are shown at the top of the browser, above where you type the URL, or on the tab for that page (if your browser uses tabs).

cards.title: Body Tag
cards.body:
Everything inside the element is shown inside the main browser window. Basic page: Hello

quiz.question: Where is the text of the <title> element displayed?
options: On the browser tab / title bar
At the bottom of the page
quiz.explanation: The title is shown in the browser's title bar or on the tab for that page.

cards.title: HTML 4.01 DOCTYPEs
cards.body: HTML 4.01 had three types. Strict: <!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/strict.dtd">. Transitional: <!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Transitional//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/loose.dtd">. Frameset: <!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Frameset//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/frameset.dtd">.

quiz.question: In which year was HTML 4.01 released?
quiz.explanation: HTML 4.01 - 1999. HTML 2.0 was 1995, XHTML 2000 and HTML 5 2014.

cards.title: HTML 5 DOCTYPE
cards.body: HTML 5 uses a very short declaration: <!DOCTYPE html>. It is an instruction to the web browser about what version of HTML the page is written in. The <!DOCTYPE> declaration is not case sensitive.

quiz.question: What is the correct HTML5 DOCTYPE?
quiz.explanation: HTML5 simply uses <!DOCTYPE html>, and it is not case sensitive.

cards.title: Head Section
cards.body: The <head> section holds information about the page rather than visible content. Elements you can place in it: <title>, <meta>, <link> and <style>. (Add-on: <base> sets the default URL/target for all links and <script> adds JavaScript.)

cards.title: Meta Tag
cards.body: <meta> tag is used to add a description of the HTML page. The description is used by search engines for indexing and ranking the web page. <meta> tags always go inside the <head> element. Character encoding for the HTML document: <meta charset="UTF-8">.

cards.title: Meta Attributes (Part 1)
cards.body: charset - character_set: specifies the character encoding. content - text: gives the value associated with the http-equiv or name attribute. http-equiv - content-type, default-style, refresh: provides an HTTP header for the information/value of the content attribute.

cards.title: Meta Attributes (Part 2)
cards.body: name - application-name, author, description, generator, keywords: specifies a name for the metadata. Example: <meta name="author" content="...">.

quiz.question: Inside which element do <meta> tags always go?
quiz.explanation: <meta> tags always go inside the <head> element.

cards.title: Description of Web Page
cards.body: Define a description of your web page: <meta name="description" content="A blog about programming language">.

cards.title: Keywords for Search Engines
cards.body: <meta name="keywords" content="HTML, C, Java, Ruby, JS, SQL">.

cards.title: Author of Web Page
cards.body: <meta name="author" content="Guwahati Section">.

cards.title: Refresh Web Page
cards.body: <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5"> refreshes the web page every 5 seconds.

quiz.question: Which meta tag reloads the page every 5 seconds?
quiz.explanation: http-equiv="refresh" with content="5" refreshes the page every 5 seconds.

cards.title: Link Tag
cards.body: The <link> tag defines a link between a document and an external resource. The <link> element is an empty element, it contains attributes only. It goes only in the head section, but it can appear any number of times.

cards.title: Link Attributes (Part 1)
cards.body: crossorigin (anonymous, use-credentials): how the element handles cross-origin requests. href (URL): location of the linked document. hreflang (language_code): language of the text in the linked document. media (media_query): on what device the linked document will be displayed.

cards.title: Link Attributes (Part 2)
cards.body: rel (required): relationship between current and linked document - alternate, archives, author, bookmark, external, first, help, icon, last, license, next, nofollow, noreferrer, pingback, prefetch, prev, search, sidebar, stylesheet, tag, up.

cards.title: Link Attributes (Part 3)
cards.body: sizes (Height x Width / any): size of the linked resource, only for rel="icon". type (media_type): media type of the linked document.

quiz.explanation: rel is required: it specifies the relationship between the current document and the linked document.

cards.title: Style Tag
cards.body: The <style> tag is used to declare style sheets within the head of an HTML document. Inside the <style> element you specify how HTML elements should render in a browser. Each HTML document can contain multiple <style> tags.

cards.title: Style Attributes
cards.body: media (media_query): what media/device the resource is optimized for. scoped (scoped): styles only apply to this element's parent element and its children. type (text/css): media type of the <style> tag.

options: In the head of the HTML document
quiz.explanation: The <style> tag declares style sheets within the head of an HTML document.

cards.body: The <hr> tag is used to create a horizontal rule on the web page. It is an empty tag. The web browser starts a horizontal rule from a new line, and any text that follows this tag is also displayed on a new line.

quiz.question: The <hr> tag is...
quiz.explanation: <hr> is an empty tag: it draws a horizontal line and has no closing tag.

quiz.question: Which tag renders text in italic style?
quiz.explanation: <i> renders italic, <b> bold and <u> underline.

cards.body: The ....... tag indicates that its content has strong importance.

quiz.explanation: <strong> marks strong importance, while <em> marks emphasis.

cards.title: Subscript
cards.body: A subscript is text that appears smaller than regular text, below the line. The <sub> ..... </sub> tag is used to create a subscript on a web page. Example: H<sub>2</sub>O.

cards.title: Superscript
cards.body: A superscript is text that appears in a smaller size above the regular text. The <sup> ...... </sup> tag is used to create a superscript on a web page. Example: x<sup>2</sup>.

quiz.question: Which tag creates H2O with a lowered '2'?
quiz.explanation: <sub> creates subscript text below the baseline.

cards.title: Ins and Del
cards.body: The <ins> ..... </ins> tag can be used to show content that has been inserted into a document, while the <del> ..... </del> tag can show text that has been deleted from it.

cards.title: The s Tag (Strikethrough)
cards.body: The <s> ....... </s> tag specifies text that is no longer correct, accurate or relevant. It is displayed with a line through it (strikethrough).

quiz.question: Which tag shows text that is no longer correct, accurate or relevant?
quiz.explanation: <s> marks text that is no longer accurate or relevant, shown with a strikethrough.

cards.title: Abbreviation and Acronym
cards.body: The <abbr> ......... </abbr> tag defines an abbreviation or an acronym. A title attribute on the opening tag is used to specify the full term. Example: <abbr title="Guwahati"> GHY </abbr> is awesome.

cards.title: Address
cards.body: The <address> ....... </address> tag is used to contain contact details for the author/owner of the page/article/web site.

quiz.question: Which tag is for short quotes that sit inside a paragraph?
quiz.explanation: <q> is for short inline quotes; <blockquote> is for long multiline quotations.

quiz.explanation: HTML comments start with <!-- and end with -->.

quiz.explanation: <ul> defines the list and <li> defines each item.

quiz.explanation: type accepts 1, A, a, I or i. type="I" gives uppercase Roman numerals.

cards.title: Definition List
cards.body: A definition list is a list of terms, with a definition of each term. We can create a definition list by using <dl> ..... </dl> with the <dt> and <dd> tags. The <dt> .... </dt> tag is used to define the term; whereas, the <dd> tag is used to give the term's definition.

cards.body: <dl><dt>College</dt><dd>A boring place</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd>Learn as much as you can</dd><dt>Railway Station</dt><dd>Too much crowded</dd></dl>

quiz.question: In a definition list, which tag defines the term?
quiz.explanation: <dt> is the term, <dd> its definition, and <dl> wraps the list.

quiz.explanation: <th> is the heading cell, <td> is the data cell and <tr> is a row.

cards.title: Border
cards.body: border="1" draws a border of 1 pixel around the table and its cells: <table border="1">. Without it, the table has no visible lines.

cards.title: Cellpadding and Cellspacing
cards.body: cellpadding sets the space between the cell's content and its border: <table cellpadding="10">. cellspacing sets the space between cells: <table cellspacing="5">.

cards.title: Width and Height
cards.body: width and height set the size of the table (or a cell) in pixels or percent: <table width="500" height="200"> or <table width="100%">. (Add-on note: these table attributes are deprecated in HTML5; the modern way is CSS border, padding, border-spacing, width and height.)

quiz.question: Which attribute sets the space between the content of a cell and its border?
quiz.explanation: cellpadding is space inside the cell; cellspacing is the space between cells.

cards.title: Colspan

cards.title: Rowspan
cards.body: rowspan merges cells down rows: Merged makes one cell take the height of 2 rows. The next row then has one cell less.

quiz.question: Which attribute makes a cell stretch across two columns?
quiz.explanation: colspan merges columns, rowspan merges rows.

element is very often used together with CSS, to lay out a web page.

cards.title: Div Behaviour
cards.body: By default, browsers always place a line break before and after the <div> element. However, this can be changed with CSS.

quiz.question: What is the <div> tag used for?
options: To define a section and group elements together
quiz.explanation: <div> groups elements into a section so they can be formatted or laid out with CSS.

cards.title: Style Attribute
cards.body: The style attribute is used to set the style of an HTML element. In HTML5, the style attribute can be used on any HTML element.

cards.title: Syntax
cards.body:
style="property1: property1-value; property2: property2-value;" where property is a CSS property and property-value is a CSS value. Example:

I am Heading

. Remember to separate properties with a semicolon.

quiz.question: How do you separate two CSS properties in a style attribute?
quiz.explanation: Each property: value pair ends with a semicolon.

cards.title: Class Attribute
cards.body: The HTML class attribute makes it possible to define equal styles for elements with the same class name. The class attribute specifies one or more class names for an element. It is mostly used to point to a class in a style sheet, but it can also be used by JavaScript (via the HTML DOM) to make changes to HTML elements with a specified class. In HTML5, class can be used on any HTML element.

cards.title: Rules
cards.body: Must begin with a letter A-Z or a-z. A class name cannot start with a number. Must not contain any space characters. Can be followed by letters (A-Za-z), digits (0-9), hyphens ("-") and underscores ("_"). In HTML, all values are case-insensitive.

cards.title: More than One Class
cards.body:
To specify multiple classes, separate the class names with a space: class="class_name1 class_name2 class_nameN". Example:

I am first paragraph

. In CSS: p.red {color: #FF0000;} p.look {font-size: 60px;} .algn {text-align: center;}

quiz.question: How do you give an element two classes?
quiz.explanation: Separate class names with a space: class="red look".

cards.title: Id Attribute
cards.body: The id attribute specifies a unique id for an HTML element. The value must be unique within the HTML document. It is most used to point to a style in a style sheet, and by JavaScript (via the HTML DOM) to manipulate the element with the specific id. The id attribute can be used on any HTML element.

cards.title: Rules and Example
cards.body:
Same rules as class: must begin with a letter, no spaces, followed by letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. CSS example: #geekyshows { color: red; font-size: 60px; } applied to

Hello World!

- other paragraphs are not affected.

quiz.question: Which statement about id is true?
options: Its value must be unique in the document
It can start with a number
Many elements can share an id
quiz.explanation: An id must be unique within the document.
