options: Connects one web page to another
quiz.explanation: A hyperlink is a link between web pages used to connect one page to another.

cards.title: Types of href
cards.body: Syntax: <a href="URL">. An absolute URL points to another web site, e.g. href="http://www.geekyshows.com". A relative URL points to a file within a web site, e.g. href="page1.html".

cards.title: Other href Values
cards.body: Link to an element with a specified id within the page: href="#bottom". Other protocols: https://, ftp://, mailto:, file:, etc. A script: href='javascript:alert("Hello");'.

quiz.question: Which href value links to an element with id 'bottom' on the same page?
quiz.explanation: A # followed by the id jumps to that element in the same page.

cards.title: What is a Named Anchor?
cards.body:
A named anchor is a target location inside a page that a link can jump to. You give an element an id, then link to it with #id. Example: Important ...

Goodwill is that unseen force which is

.

cards.title: Go to Top Example
cards.body:
Important

Once upon a time, all the birds - the swans, cranes,

Goodwill is that unseen force which is

He has neither the time, nor the interest to bother

Go to Top. (Add-on: the old way used ; the id attribute replaces it in HTML5.)

quiz.question:
How do you create a link that jumps back to

?
quiz.explanation: Use href="#top" where top is the id of the target element.

cards.title: Attribute Table
cards.body: href (URL) - specifies the URL as destination web page or different section of the web page. download (filename) - the target will be downloaded when a user clicks the hyperlink. media (media_query) - what media/device the linked document is optimized for. hreflang (language_code) - language of the linked document. type (media_type) - media type of the linked document.

cards.title: Download Attribute
cards.body: The download attribute specifies that the target will be downloaded when a user clicks on the hyperlink. Example: <a href="/images/example.jpg" download="guwahatisection">.

quiz.question: Which attribute makes the browser download the file on click?
quiz.explanation: The download attribute makes the target download instead of opening.

cards.title: Target Values
cards.body: _blank - opens the linked document in a new window or tab. _parent - opens in the parent frame. _top - opens in the full body of the window. framename - opens in a named frame. _self - opens in the same frame as it was clicked (this is the default).

cards.title: Example
cards.body: Visit Guwahatisection

quiz.question: Which target value opens the link in a new tab or window?
quiz.explanation: _blank opens a new window or tab; _self (default) uses the same frame.

cards.title: Purpose
cards.body: The rel attribute specifies the relationship between the current document and the linked document. Example: GuwahatiSection.

cards.title: rel Values (Part 1)
cards.body: alternate - alternate version (print page, translated or mirror). author - link to the author. bookmark - permanent URL for bookmarking. help - help document. license - copyright information. next - next document in a selection.

cards.title: rel Values (Part 2)
cards.body: nofollow - unendorsed document, like a paid link (Google's spider should not follow it). noreferrer - browser should not send an HTTP referer header. prefetch - target document should be cached. prev - previous document. search - search tool for the document. tag - a keyword for the current document.

quiz.question: What does rel="nofollow" tell search engines?
options: Open the link in a new tab
quiz.explanation: nofollow links to an unendorsed document; Google's spider should not follow it.

cards.title: Default Link Colors
cards.body: By default, links appear as follows in all browsers: an unvisited link is underlined and blue, a visited link is underlined and purple, and an active link is underlined and red.

cards.title: link, vlink, alink
cards.body: link - specifies the color of a hyperlink that has not been visited or clicked before. vlink - the color of a hyperlink that has been visited. alink - the color of currently active links. (Add-on: these are <body> attributes in old HTML; today use CSS a:link, a:visited and a:active.)

quiz.question: By default, what colour is a visited link?
quiz.explanation: Unvisited = blue, visited = purple, active = red.

cards.title: Language Codes
cards.body: English - en, Hindi - hi, Bengali - bn, Gujarati - gu, Kashmiri - ks, Marathi - mr, Malayalam - ml, Punjabi - pa, Sanskrit - sa, Tamil - ta, Telugu - te, Oriya - or, Sindhi - sd, Kannada - kn, Arabic - ar, Nepali - ne, Japanese - ja, French - fr, Indonesian - id/in, Korean - ko, Portuguese - pt, Russian - ru. Example: hreflang="en".

cards.title: Type Attribute
cards.body: The type attribute gives the media type of the linked document. The list of media types is at http://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml.

quiz.question: What is the hreflang code for Hindi?
quiz.explanation: Hindi = hi, English = en, Bengali = bn.

cards.title: Media Attribute
cards.body: The media attribute specifies what media/device the linked document is optimized for. It is used to specify that the target URL is designed for special devices (like iPhone, Android etc.), speech or print media.

cards.title: Media Values (1): Part 1
cards.body: width - width of the targeted display area. Example: media="screen and (min-width:500px)". height - height of the display area. Example: media="screen and (max-height:700px)". device-width - width of the target display/paper.

cards.title: Media Values (1): Part 2
cards.body: device-height - height of the target display/paper. orientation - portrait or landscape. Example: media="all and (orientation: landscape)". ("min-" and "max-" prefixes can be used with width, height, device-width and device-height.)

cards.title: Media Values (2)
cards.body: aspect-ratio - width/height ratio of the targeted display area, e.g. media="screen and (aspect-ratio:16/9)". device-aspect-ratio - device-width/device-height ratio. color - bits per color of target display. color-index - number of colors the display can handle. monochrome - bits per pixel in a monochrome frame buffer.

cards.title: Media Values (3) & Media Types
cards.body: resolution - pixel density (dpi or dpcm), e.g. media="print and (resolution:300dpi)". scan - scanning method of a TV: progressive or interlace. grid - 1 for grid, 0 otherwise. Media types: all (default), aural, braille, handheld, projection, print (print preview/printed pages), screen (computer screens), tty, tv. Operators: and, not, "," (OR).

quiz.question: Which media type targets printed pages?
quiz.explanation: print is for print preview mode and printed pages; screen is for computer screens.

cards.title: The Tag
cards.body: The tag is used to insert an image in web pages. Attributes: src (URL) - URL of an image. alt (text) - alternate text for an image. width (pixels) - width of an image. height (pixels) - height of an image. ismap - specifies an image as a server-side image-map. usemap (#mapname) - specifies an image as a client-side image-map.

cards.title: src Attribute
cards.body: or with a full path . (Add-on: a local path like C:\ only works on your own computer; use relative paths in real websites.)

cards.title: alt, width and height
cards.body: alt: . Width and height: .

quiz.question: Which attribute provides alternate text for an image?
quiz.explanation: alt gives alternate text when the image cannot be shown and helps screen readers.

cards.title: ismap Attribute
cards.body: With ismap, the click coordinates are sent to the server.

cards.title: Map Tag
cards.body: The <map> .... </map> tag is used to define a client-side image-map. An image-map is an image with clickable areas. The <map> tag contains a number of <area> tags that define the clickable areas. Syntax: <map name="mapname" id="mapname"> ......... </map>.

cards.title: Area Tag
cards.body: The <area> tag defines an area inside an image-map. The <area> element is always nested inside a <map> ... </map> tag.

quiz.question: Where must the <area> element be placed?
quiz.explanation: <area> is always nested inside a <map> tag.

cards.title: Area Attributes
cards.body: alt (text) - alternate text, required if href is present. coords - coordinates of the area. download - download the target. href - hyperlink target. hreflang - language. media - media/device. shape - default, rect, circle, poly. target - _blank, _parent, _self, _top, framename. type - media type. rel - relationship with the target URL.

cards.title: Coords Values
cards.body: rect: x, y, x1, y1 - left, top, right, bottom corner of the rectangle. circle: x, y, radius - centre and radius. poly: x, y, x1, y1, ..., xn, yn - edges of the polygon; if the first and last coordinate pairs are not the same, the browser adds the last pair to close the polygon.

quiz.question: How are the coords of a circle given?
quiz.explanation: A circle uses centre x, y and the radius.

cards.title: Audio Tag
cards.body: The <audio> .... </audio> tag defines sound, such as music or other audio streams. Supported formats: mp3, wav and ogg.

cards.title: Audio Attributes
cards.body: autoplay - audio starts playing as soon as it is ready. controls - displays audio controls (play/pause etc.). loop - starts again every time it is finished. muted - audio output is muted. preload - auto, metadata, none. src (URL) - URL of the audio file.

cards.title: preload Values
cards.body: auto - the browser should load the entire audio file when the page loads. metadata - load only metadata. none - the browser should NOT load the audio file when the page loads.

quiz.question: Which attribute displays play/pause buttons for audio?
quiz.explanation: controls shows the audio controls such as play/pause.

cards.title: Video Tag
cards.body: The <video> .... </video> tag is used to play video files. Supports: MP4, ogg, WebM.

cards.title: Video Attributes
cards.body: autoplay - plays automatically on loading. controls - displays controls such as a play button. height (pixels) - height of the player. loop - starts over again when finished. muted - mutes the audio. poster (URL) - image shown while the video is downloading or until the user hits play. preload - auto, metadata, none. src (URL) - URL of the video file. width (pixels) - width of the player.

quiz.question: Which attribute shows an image until the user hits play?
quiz.explanation: poster specifies the image shown while the video is downloading or before play.

cards.title: Source Tag
cards.body: The <source> tag is used to embed two or more audio or video files of different media types. The browser may choose the file to play based on its media type or codec support. Structure: <audio><source><source></audio>.

cards.title: Source Attributes
cards.body: src (URL) - path of the file to play. type (media type) - media type of the file, e.g. type="audio/mp3". media (media query) - device the file is optimized for.

cards.title: Media Types
cards.body: Audio: MP3 - audio/mpeg or audio/mp3, Ogg - audio/ogg, Wav - audio/wav. Video: MP4 - video/mp4, WebM - video/webm, Ogg - video/ogg. More at http://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml.

quiz.question: What is the media type for an MP4 video?
quiz.explanation: MP4 = video/mp4, WebM = video/webm, Ogg = video/ogg.

cards.title: Embed Tag
cards.body: The <embed> tag is used to embed an audio or video file on a web page. The <embed> tag defines a container for an external application or interactive content (a plug-in). Attributes: src (path of the file), type (media type), height (pixels), width (pixels).

cards.title: Noembed Tag
cards.body: The <noembed> .... </noembed> tag is used to handle browsers which do not support the <embed> tag. The message inside appears only when the browser doesn't support <embed>. This tag has been deprecated and should not be used in production.

quiz.question: What is <noembed> used for?
options: A message for browsers that do not support <embed>
quiz.explanation: <noembed> shows a message when <embed> is not supported; it is deprecated.

cards.title: Object Tag
cards.body: The <object> .... </object> tag is used to embed an object within an HTML document, e.g. audio, video, Java applets, ActiveX, PDF and Flash. It can also embed another web page into an HTML document. The text between <object> and </object> is alternate text for browsers that do not support this tag.

cards.title: Object Attributes
cards.body: data (URL) - URL of the resource used by the object. type (media type) - type of the data. name - name for the object. height, width (pixels). usemap (#mapname) - client-side image map. form (form_id) - forms the object belongs to.

cards.title: Param Tag
cards.body: <param> is used to pass parameters to plugins embedded with the <object> tag. Attributes: name (autoplay, width, height, src etc.) and value (true, false, 400, 200, raaz.mp4 etc.).

quiz.question: Which tag passes parameters to an <object>?
quiz.explanation: <param> passes parameters (name/value) to plugins embedded with <object>.

cards.title: Iframe Tag (Add-on)
cards.body: An <iframe> embeds another web page inside the current page. Syntax: <iframe src="URL" width="500" height="300"></iframe>. Common uses: embedding a YouTube video or a Google Map. The name attribute lets links open inside it using target="framename".

cards.title: Sandbox (Part 1)
cards.body: Sandbox is a restriction to the content, such as disabling scripts or plugins, given by the internal frame. An iframe with an empty sandbox value has these restrictions: forms cannot be submitted; the framed document cannot navigate its top-level parent; scripts are disabled; plugins are stopped.

cards.title: Sandbox (Part 2)
cards.body: New windows cannot be created; the framed content is treated as from a unique origin so it has no access to earlier cookies; APIs are disabled; automatically triggered features like auto-playing videos are blocked. Syntax: <iframe sandbox> </iframe>.

quiz.question: What does an iframe with an empty sandbox attribute do?
quiz.explanation: A sandbox with no value applies all restrictions.

cards.title: Values Table
cards.body: (no value) - applies all restrictions. allow-forms - re-enables form submission. allow-pointer-lock - re-enables APIs. allow-popups - re-enables popups. allow-same-origin - allows the content to be treated as being from the same origin. allow-scripts - re-enables scripts. allow-top-navigation - allows the content to navigate its top-level browsing context.

cards.title: allow-same-origin
cards.body: A web page can have access to a second web page only if both have the same origin: the same URI scheme, port number and host name. http://www.geekyshows.com/p/contact-us.html and http://www.geekyshows.com/p/about-us.html - same origin. http://www.geekyshows.com:82/... - different port, so not the same origin. http://en.www.geekyshows.com/... - different host, so not the same origin.

cards.title: allow-top-navigation
cards.body: Top navigation allows us to open the linked document in the full body of the window or the top browsing context. Target values: _blank (new window or tab), _parent (parent frame), _top (full body of the window), framename (named frame), _self (same frame, default).

quiz.question: Which sandbox value re-enables scripts?
quiz.explanation: allow-scripts re-enables scripts inside a sandboxed iframe.

cards.title: What are Frames?
cards.body: Frames divide the browser window into several sections, each showing a separate HTML document. They were used in HTML 4.01 (the Frameset DOCTYPE). In a frameset page there is no <body> - the <frameset> replaces it.

cards.title: Frameset Syntax
cards.body: <frameset cols="30%,70%"><frame src="menu.html"><frame src="content.html"></frameset> splits the window into two columns. Use rows="..." for horizontal sections. <frame> is an empty tag with src, name, scrolling and noresize attributes. <noframes> gives text for browsers that do not support frames.

cards.title: Note
cards.body: <frameset> and <frame> are not supported in HTML5. Use <iframe> or CSS layout instead - but they are part of your syllabus and appear in older sites.

quiz.question: Which tag defines how the browser window is divided into frames?
quiz.explanation: <frameset> with rows or cols divides the window; each <frame> loads one document.

cards.title: Nested Frameset
cards.body: A frameset can be placed inside another frameset to create complex layouts. Example: <frameset cols="25%,75%"><frame src="menu.html"><frameset rows="20%,80%"><frame src="top.html"><frame src="main.html"></frameset></frameset> - a left menu column and, in the right column, a top part above a main part.

cards.title: Linking into a Frame
cards.body: Give a frame a name - - and open links in it with target: Page 2.

quiz.question: How do you open a link inside a frame named "content"?
quiz.explanation: Use the target attribute with the frame's name.

units.title: Module 2.2: Forms & HTML5
units.description: HTML forms, input types and validation, plus HTML5 semantic elements, new tags and page layout.

modules.title: HTML Forms & Validation
modules.description: Form tag, attributes, GET vs POST, input types and attributes, textarea, dropdowns, buttons and HTML5 validation.

cards.title: Form Tag
cards.body: HTML forms are used to collect some data from the site visitor. The HTML <form> ..... </form> tag is used to create an HTML form.

cards.title: Form Elements
cards.body: Elements used inside a form: <input>, <textarea>, <button>, <select>, <option>, <optgroup>, <fieldset>, <label>.

quiz.question: What are HTML forms used for?
options: Collecting data from the site visitor
quiz.explanation: Forms collect data from the site visitor.

cards.title: Attribute Table (1)
cards.body: accept-charset (UTF-8) - charset used in the submitted form (default: the page charset). action (URL) - where to send the data after submitting the form. autocomplete (on default / off) - whether the browser retains the history of previous values. enctype - how the browser encodes the data before it sends it to the server (default: url-encoded).

cards.title: Attribute Table (2)
cards.body: method (GET default / POST) - how to send the form data to a web server; as URL variables with get or as HTTP post. name - a name used to identify the form. novalidate - the browser should not validate the form. target (_self default, _blank, _parent, _top, framename) - target of the address in the action attribute.

quiz.question: Which form attribute defines where the data is sent?
quiz.explanation: action contains the URL that receives the form data.

cards.title: accept-charset
cards.body: It specifies the character encodings used for the form submission. ISO-8859-1 - character encoding for the Latin alphabet. UTF-8 - character encoding for Unicode. Example: <form accept-charset="UTF-8">.

cards.title: Action Attribute (Part 1)
cards.body: It contains a URL that defines where to send the data after submitting the form. It specifies the physical address of the server to which the user data should be redirected at the click of the submit button.

cards.title: Action Attribute (Part 2)
cards.body: Examples: action="http://www.something.com/something.html", action="page.html", action="gotform.php", action="example.asp". If the action attribute is omitted, the action is set to the current page.

cards.title: Autocomplete
cards.body: On - the browser will automatically complete values based on values the user has entered before. Off - the user needs to write all values each time they fill the form. Example: <form autocomplete="on">.

quiz.question: What happens if the action attribute is omitted?
options: The action is set to the current page
quiz.explanation: If action is omitted, the data is sent to the current page.

cards.title: Encoding Values (Part 1)
cards.body: enctype specifies how the browser encodes the data before it sends it to the server. application/x-www-form-urlencoded - all characters are encoded before sending (spaces become "+" symbols and special characters are converted to ASCII HEX values).

cards.title: Encoding Values (Part 2)
cards.body: multipart/form-data - no characters are encoded; required when you use forms that have a file upload control. text/plain - spaces are converted to "+" symbols, but no special characters are encoded.

cards.title: Example
cards.body: <form enctype="multipart/form-data">

quiz.question: Which enctype is required for file upload forms?
quiz.explanation: multipart/form-data is required when the form has a file upload control.

cards.title: Method Attribute
cards.body: The method attribute specifies how to send the form data to a web server. The data can be sent as URL variables, by using the get method, or as HTTP post, by using the post method. GET is the default.

cards.title: GET Features (Part 1)
cards.body: GET sends the data as part of the URL. It appends form-data into the URL in name/value pairs. The length of a URL is limited to 2048 characters. Never use GET if you have a password or other sensitive information. Useful for submissions where a user wants to bookmark the result.

cards.title: GET Features (Part 2)
cards.body: Better for non-secure data, like query strings in Google. GET can't be used to send binary data, e.g. images or Word documents. Example: <form action="some.php" method="GET">. If we use an invalid value for the method attribute, the browser will use the default value GET.

quiz.question: Why should GET never be used for passwords?
options: The data is visible in the URL
GET does not work with forms
quiz.explanation: GET appends data to the URL, so it is visible to everyone.

cards.title: POST Features
cards.body: HTTP POST requests supply additional data from the client (browser) to the server in the message body. It appends form-data inside the body of the HTTP request (data is not shown in the URL). The POST method has no restriction on the size of data sent. Form submissions with POST cannot be bookmarked. POST can send ASCII as well as binary data, e.g. images and Word documents.

cards.title: POST Security
cards.body: The data sent by POST goes through the HTTP header so security depends on the HTTP protocol; by using secure HTTP you can make sure your information is secure. POST is a little safer than GET because the parameters are not stored in browser history or in web server logs. Example: <form action="some.php" method="POST">.

quiz.question: Which method can send binary data such as images?
quiz.explanation: POST has no size restriction and can send ASCII as well as binary data.

cards.title: Comparison Table (1)
cards.body: BACK button/Reload: GET - harmless; POST - data will be re-submitted (the browser should alert the user). Bookmarked: GET - can be bookmarked; POST - cannot. Cached: GET - can be cached; POST - not cached.

cards.title: Comparison Table (2): Part 1
cards.body: Encoding type: GET - application/x-www-form-urlencoded; POST - application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data (use multipart for binary data). History: GET - parameters remain in browser history; POST - not saved.

cards.title: Comparison Table (2): Part 2
cards.body: Restrictions on data type: GET - only ASCII characters; POST - no restrictions, binary allowed. Visibility: GET - data is visible to everyone in the URL; POST - data is not displayed in the URL.

quiz.question: Which method keeps parameters in the browser history?
quiz.explanation: GET parameters remain in browser history; POST parameters are not saved.

cards.title: Name Attribute
cards.body: name specifies a name used to identify the form. It is also used to give a name to a control, which is sent to the server so the value can be recognized. Example: name="lastname".

cards.title: novalidate
cards.body: If we use the novalidate attribute in the form tag then validation will not take place, even if there is a required field. Examples: <form novalidate>, <form novalidate="novalidate">, <form novalidate="true">. There is one more attribute, formnovalidate, which is used by the input tag to apply novalidate to that particular field.

quiz.question: What does novalidate do on a <form>?
quiz.explanation: With novalidate the browser does not validate, even required fields.

cards.title: Input Tag
cards.body: The <input> tag prompts the user to enter data and also requests information from the web server after submitting the web form. Syntax: <form><input></form>. There is no input end tag in HTML5.

cards.title: Type Attribute
cards.body: The type attribute indicates the type of input element. It is an empty tag. The default value is text. Example: <input> or <input type="text">.

quiz.question: What is the default input type?
quiz.explanation: If no type is given, the input is a text field.

cards.title: accept to disabled (Part 1)
cards.body: accept - file types the server accepts (file_extension, audio/*, video/*, image/*, media_type). alt - alternate text for an image, only with type="image". autocomplete - on/off. autofocus - the input gets focus when the page loads.

cards.title: accept to disabled (Part 2)
cards.body: checked - input is checked on load; only with checkbox and radio. dirname - the text direction will be submitted (inputname.dir). disabled - disables the input; cannot be used with type="hidden".

cards.title: form to formaction
cards.body: form (form_id) - the form's id to which the input belongs. formaction (URL) - the file that will process the input when the form is submitted.

quiz.question: Which attribute pre-selects a checkbox or radio button on load?
quiz.explanation: checked works only with type="checkbox" and type="radio".

cards.title: Form Overrides
cards.body: formenctype - application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, text/plain: how form-data is encoded. formmethod - GET/POST. formnovalidate - form elements should not be validated on submit. formtarget - _blank, _self, _parent, _top, framename: where to display the response. height - height of an input field. list - id of a <datalist> containing options.

cards.title: Limits & Hints (Part 1)
cards.body: max / min - maximum and minimum value for number, range, date, datetime-local, month, time and week. maxlength / minlength - maximum/minimum number of characters in a text field. multiple - more than one value allowed. name - unique name for the input.

cards.title: Limits & Hints (Part 2)
cards.body: pattern - a regular expression the value is checked against. placeholder - a short hint of the expected value (text, search, url, tel, email, password). readonly - value cannot be modified. required - must be filled out before submitting. size - width of the control (in characters for text/password).

cards.title: Remaining Attributes
cards.body: src (URL) - image to display, only with type="image". step - legal number intervals. type - the input type. value - value of the input. width - width of the input field.

quiz.question: Which attribute shows a short hint inside an empty input?
quiz.explanation: placeholder specifies a short hint describing the expected value.

lessons.title: Input Types: Text, Password, Button, Email

cards.title: Text & Password
cards.body: Text - defines a single-line text field: <input type="text">. Password - like a text field, but hides each typed character by displaying an asterisk (*) or bullets instead: <input type="password">.

cards.title: Button & Email
cards.body: Button - adds a button on a web form to activate a script when the user clicks it: <input type="button">. Email - adds an email address or list of email addresses; the format should be like example@gmail.com else it will prompt an error: <input type="email">.

quiz.question: Which input type hides typed characters with bullets?
quiz.explanation: type="password" displays asterisks or bullets instead of the characters.

cards.title: Check Box
cards.body: A check box is a small box which, when selected, includes a checkmark. It is used to allow the user to select one or more than one of the options available. A user can select or clear the check box by clicking it. <input type="checkbox">.

cards.title: Radio Button
cards.body: A radio button is used to create a series of options of which only one can be selected. It is displayed as a circle which, when selected, displays a dot in the middle. <input type="radio">. (Add-on: give all radio buttons in a group the same name.)

cards.title: URL, Autofocus & Pattern
cards.body: URL - used to enter only web addresses in their correct format; if not entered correctly the field validates the text. <input type="url">. Autofocus - keeps the focus on the input field. Pattern - defines the regular expression of the text that should be entered in the text field.

quiz.question: Which control allows selecting only ONE option from a series?
quiz.explanation: Radio buttons allow only one choice; checkboxes allow one or more.

lessons.title: Input Types: Search, Tel, Range, Number

cards.title: Search & Tel
cards.body: Search Box - adds a search box to a form: <input type="search">. Tel - a one-line plain-text edit for entering a telephone number: <input type="tel">.

cards.title: Range & Number
cards.body: Range - represents the input of limited-range numerical values: <input type="range">. Number - validates the textbox only if the value within the field is numerical: <input type="number">.

quiz.question: Which type accepts only numerical values?
quiz.explanation: type="number" validates that the value is numeric.

cards.title: File
cards.body: File - used to upload a file on a web page. You also need to set enctype="multipart/form-data". <input type="file">.

cards.title: Image
cards.body: Image - represents either an image from which the user can interactively select a pair of coordinates and submit the form, or alternatively a button from which the user can submit the form. <input type="image">.

cards.title: Hidden
cards.body: Hidden - stores data that is not visible to the user on a web page. It is used to submit some information that cannot be edited by the user. <input type="hidden">.

quiz.question: Which input type stores data that the user cannot see?
quiz.explanation: type="hidden" submits data without showing it on the page.

cards.title: Submit
cards.body: A submit button is used to transfer form data to the URL specified in the <form action> tag. <input type="submit">.

cards.title: Reset
cards.body: A reset button helps the user to clear all the data that they have entered in the text fields. <input type="reset">.

quiz.question: Which button clears all data entered in the form?
quiz.explanation: type="reset" restores the form fields to their initial values.

lessons.title: Input Types: Date, Time, Month, Week, Color

cards.title: Date & Time
cards.body: Date - for input fields that should contain a date: <input type="date">. Time - allows the user to select a time: <input type="time">. DateTime - allows selecting date and time: <input type="datetime">. Datetime-local - allows selecting a date and time: <input type="datetime-local">. (Add-on: datetime is obsolete; use datetime-local.)

cards.title: Month, Week & Color
cards.body: Month - select a month and year: <input type="month">. Week - select a week and year: <input type="week">. Color - for input fields that should contain a color: <input type="color">.

cards.title: Min and Max & Text Direction
cards.body: min and max work with number, range, date, datetime-local, month, time and week. dirname specifies the text direction submitted; text direction values: ltr (default, left-to-right), rtl (right-to-left), auto (browser decides). Example: <input type="text" name="city" dirname="city.dir">.

quiz.question: Which type lets the user pick a month and year?
quiz.explanation: type="month" selects a month and year; type="week" selects a week and year.

cards.title: Text Area
cards.body: A text area is a multiline text field. A user can write an unlimited number of characters in the text area. <textarea> ...... </textarea>.

cards.title: Textarea Attributes
cards.body: autofocus - gets focus on page load. cols (number) - visible width. dirname - text direction submitted. disabled. form (form_id). maxlength (number). name (text). placeholder (text). readonly. required. rows (number) - visible number of lines. wrap (soft default / hard) - how text is wrapped when submitted.

cards.title: wrap Values
cards.body: soft - the text in the textarea is not wrapped when submitted in a form. hard - the text in the textarea is wrapped (contains newlines) when submitted. When "hard" is used, the cols attribute must be specified.

quiz.question: Which attribute sets the visible number of lines in a textarea?
quiz.explanation: rows sets the visible lines; cols sets the visible width.

cards.title: Label
cards.body: Label defines a set of text that is associated with a particular element. <label> ..... </label>. Attributes: for (element_id) - which form element a label is bound to; form (form_id) - forms the label belongs to. element_id is the id of the element the label is bound to.

cards.title: Fieldset
cards.body: Fieldset creates a box around the related form controls. <fieldset> ...... </fieldset>. Attributes: disabled - a group of related form elements is disabled; form (form_id); name (text).

cards.title: Legend
cards.body: Legend defines a caption for the fieldset element. <fieldset><legend> ....... </legend></fieldset>.

quiz.question: Which tag gives a caption to a <fieldset>?
quiz.explanation: <legend> is the caption for a fieldset.

cards.title: Select Tag
cards.body: The <select> .... </select> tag creates a drop-down list to accept user input from a list of items. Attributes: autofocus, disabled, form (form_id), multiple (multiple options can be selected), name, required, size (number of visible options).

cards.title: Option Tag
cards.body: The <option> ... </option> tags inside <select> define an option in the drop-down list. Attributes: disabled; label (shorter label); selected (pre-selected on load); value (value sent to the server).

cards.title: Optgroup Tag
cards.body: The <optgroup> .... </optgroup> tag helps to group related choices when we have a long list of options in a <select>. Attributes: disabled; label - a label for the option-group.

quiz.question: Which attribute pre-selects an <option> when the page loads?
quiz.explanation: selected pre-selects an option; checked is for checkboxes and radios.

cards.title: Button Tag
cards.body: We can customize the appearance of a button using the <button> ..... </button> tag.

cards.title: Button Attributes
cards.body: autofocus; disabled; form (form_id); formaction (URL, only type="submit"); formenctype; formmethod (get/post); formnovalidate; formtarget; name; type (button, reset, submit); value (initial value).

quiz.question: Which values can the type attribute of <button> take?
quiz.explanation: A <button> can be type button, reset or submit.

cards.title: Datalist
cards.body: The datalist tag provides an autocomplete feature, which means it allows you to select an input from predefined options. The datalist tag is combined with the input tag. Structure: <datalist><option>......</option><option>......</option></datalist>. (Add-on: link them with <input list="id"> and <datalist id="id">.)

quiz.question: What does <datalist> provide?
quiz.explanation: <datalist> gives predefined options as autocomplete for an input.

cards.title: Required & Autofocus
cards.body: required - the field must be filled out before the form can be submitted: <input type="text" required>. autofocus - places the cursor in the field when the page loads: <input type="text" autofocus>.

cards.title: Pattern Attribute
cards.body: pattern checks the value against a regular expression. Example: <input type="text" pattern="[0-9]{10}" title="Enter a 10 digit number"> accepts exactly 10 digits. The title text is shown in the error message.

cards.title: email, number, date & range
cards.body: type="email" checks for a valid email format. type="number" accepts numbers only, with min, max and step: <input type="number" min="1" max="10">. type="date" gives a date picker with min/max dates. type="range" gives a slider with min, max and step: <input type="range" min="0" max="100" step="10">.

quiz.question: Which attribute checks the value against a regular expression?
quiz.explanation: pattern validates the input against a regex, e.g. [0-9]{10} for a 10-digit number.

modules.title: HTML5, Semantic Tags & Layout
modules.description: HTML5 introduction, new structure elements, new tags, meter, progress, dialog and page layout.

cards.title: What is HTML 5?
cards.body: HTML 5 enables us to create more interactive websites by embedding audio, video and graphics on the web page. The purpose of HTML5 is primarily to make it easier for web developers.

cards.title: New Features
cards.body: Browser Support, Geolocation, Offline Application Cache, Web Storage, Error Handling, New Application Programming Interface (API), New Structure.

cards.title: DOCTYPE in HTML 5
cards.body: HTML 5 uses the simple declaration <!DOCTYPE html>.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of HTML5?
options: To make things easier for web developers and add audio, video and graphics
quiz.explanation: HTML5 makes it easier for developers and enables interactive sites with audio, video and graphics.

cards.title: New APIs
cards.body: New Application Programming Interfaces in HTML5 include: 2D drawing on a web page, Drag and Drop, Timed Media Playback, Browser History Management.

cards.title: Other Features (Add-on)
cards.body: Geolocation finds the visitor's location (with permission). Web Storage (localStorage and sessionStorage) saves data in the browser. The offline application cache lets pages work without an internet connection.

quiz.question: Which of these is an HTML5 API?
quiz.explanation: Drag and Drop, 2D drawing, Timed Media Playback and History Management are HTML5 APIs.

cards.title: New Structure Tags
cards.body: HTML5 introduces new structure tags such as <article>, <aside>, <header>, <details>, <dialog> and more.

cards.title: HTML 5 Tags List
cards.body: <article>, <aside>, <details>, <header>, <footer>, <nav>, <section>, <summary>, <meter>, <progress>, <rp>, <rt>, <rb>, <rtc>, <ruby>, <time>, <menu>, <menuitem>, <bdi>, <mark>, <output>, <dialog>, <main>, <wbr>, <canvas>, <figcaption>, <figure>, <track>, <template>, <audio>, <video>, <data>, <datalist>, <source>, <embed>.

quiz.question: Which of these is a new HTML5 structure tag?
quiz.explanation: <article> is new in HTML5; <font>, <center> and <frameset> are old/deprecated.

cards.title: Header
cards.body: Header - it specifies a header for a document or section.

cards.title: Nav
cards.body: Nav - it defines navigation links.

cards.title: Section
cards.body: Section - it defines a section in a document.

quiz.question: Which tag defines navigation links?
quiz.explanation: <nav> is used for navigation links.

cards.title: Article
cards.body: Article - it defines an article, for example a blog post or forum post.

cards.title: Aside
cards.body: Aside - it can define content aside from the page content, like a sidebar.

cards.title: Footer
cards.body: Footer - it specifies a footer for a document or section.

quiz.question: Which tag is used for a sidebar?
quiz.explanation: <aside> defines content aside from the main page content, like a sidebar.

cards.title: Details
cards.body: Details - it is used to define additional details that the user can view or hide. It has one attribute-value pair, open="open", which means that by default the data will be visible to users. By default it has a false value, so the details will be hidden.

cards.title: Summary
cards.body: Summary - it is used to define a visible heading for a <details> element. Example (Add-on): <details><summary>Click me</summary>Hidden text</details>.

quiz.question: Which tag gives a visible heading to <details>?
quiz.explanation: <summary> is the visible heading of a <details> element.

cards.title: Meter Tag
cards.body: It defines a scalar measurement within a known range, or a fraction value. This is also known as a gauge. It should not be used to indicate a progress bar. If the browser doesn't support the meter tag then it will show the text written between the opening and closing meter tags.

cards.title: Examples
cards.body: <meter value="20" max="100" min="10">Range</meter> and <meter low="60" high="80" value="100" max="100">Range</meter>

cards.title: Meter Attributes
cards.body: value (number) - current value; must be between min and max. form (form_id) - associates the meter with a form. high - range considered high; must be less than max. low - range considered low; must be greater than min. max - maximum value. min - minimum value. optimum - the optimal value for the meter.

quiz.question: Which attribute sets the current value of a <meter>?
quiz.explanation: value is the current measurement and must be between min and max.

cards.title: Mark
cards.body:
Mark - this tag is used to highlight text or part of the text. Example:

This is Guwahatisection

.

cards.title: Dialog
cards.body: Dialog - this tag defines a dialog box or window. It can be used to create popup dialogs. It has one attribute-value pair, open="open", meaning the data will be visible by default. By default it has a false value so the data will be hidden. Example: <dialog>Click Here</dialog>.

cards.title: Main (Part 1)
cards.body: Main - this tag specifies the main content of a document. The content inside <main> should be unique to the document. It should not contain content repeated across documents such as sidebars, navigation links, copyright information, site logos and search forms.

cards.title: Main (Part 2)
cards.body: There must not be more than one <main> element in a document. <main> must NOT be a descendant of <article>, <aside>, <footer>, <header> or <nav>. Example: <main><article>This is art</article></main>.

quiz.question: How many <main> elements may a document have?
quiz.explanation: There must not be more than one <main> element in a document.

cards.title: wbr
cards.body:
wbr - the (Word Break Opportunity) element specifies a position within text where the browser may optionally break a line if necessary. Example:

Hello Guwahatishows

.

cards.title: Figure
cards.body: figure - the

cards.title: Figcaption
cards.body: figcaption - the

quiz.question: Which tag defines a caption for a <figure>?
quiz.explanation: <figcaption> is the caption for <figure>, placed as its first or last child.

cards.title: Progress Tag
cards.body: The <progress> element represents the completion progress of a task. It has two attributes: max, which specifies how much work the task requires in total, and value, which specifies how much of the task has been completed. It must be a valid floating point number between 0 and max, or between 0 and 1 if the max attribute is not present.

cards.title: Example
cards.body: <progress id="bar" value="0" max="100"> </progress>

quiz.question: Which two attributes does <progress> use?
quiz.explanation: <progress> uses max (total work) and value (work completed).

cards.title: Layout with Semantic Tags
cards.body: A typical HTML5 page layout: <header> (logo and title), <nav> (menu links), <main> containing <section>/<article> blocks and an <aside> sidebar, and finally <footer>. Skeleton: <body><header>...</header><nav>...</nav><main><section>...</section><aside>...</aside></main><footer>...</footer></body>.

cards.title: Layout with Div and Table
cards.body: Before HTML5, layouts used <div> blocks styled with CSS, e.g. <div id="header">, <div id="menu">, <div id="content">, <div id="footer">. Tables were also used for layout in the past, but they are meant for tabular data only. Modern CSS (Flexbox, Grid) is used to position the blocks side by side.

quiz.question: Which tag should hold the sidebar in an HTML5 layout?
quiz.explanation: <aside> holds content aside from the main content, such as a sidebar.

cards.title: Update Yourself
cards.body: After HTML and HTML5, the next topics to learn are: Update Yourself, CSS and Bootstrap.

quiz.question: What is the next topic to learn after HTML?
quiz.explanation: Next: CSS, then Bootstrap.

units.title: Module 3: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets)
units.description: Complete CSS course — selectors, properties, lists, tables, menus, galleries, layout, Flexbox and advanced CSS.

modules.title: Introduction & Types of CSS
modules.description: What CSS is, how a rule is written, and the three ways to attach styles to a web page.

cards.title: What is CSS?
cards.body: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) describes how HTML elements look — colors, fonts, spacing and layout — keeping presentation separate from content. One style sheet can control many pages at once, so changing a single file restyles an entire website. CSS has evolved through CSS1, CSS2 and the modular CSS3.

cards.title: CSS Syntax
cards.body: A CSS rule has the form 'selector { property: value; }'. The selector picks the HTML element, the property names what to change, and the value says how, e.g. 'p { color: red; font-size: 22px; }'. Several declarations can sit inside one pair of braces, each ending with a semicolon.

quiz.question: In the rule 'h1 { color: blue; }', what is 'color'?
quiz.explanation: 'h1' is the selector, 'color' is the property being changed, and 'blue' is the value assigned to that property.

cards.title: External Style Sheet
cards.body: An external style sheet is a separate .css file that contains only CSS rules (no HTML tags). It is linked inside <head> with <link rel='stylesheet' href='style.css'>. Changing that one file restyles every page that links to it, which makes it the best choice for whole websites.

cards.title: Internal & Inline Styles
cards.body: Internal CSS lives in a

quiz.question: Which type of CSS is best for styling an entire multi-page website from one place?
quiz.explanation: An external .css file can be linked from every page, so a single edit updates the whole site.

cards.title: Priority of Style Sheets
cards.body: When rules conflict, inline styles beat internal and external style sheets, which in turn beat the browser defaults. Internal and external sheets carry equal weight, so the one that appears later wins: a <style> block placed after the <link> overrides it, while a <style> block placed before the <link> loses.

cards.title: Comments & Multiple Style Sheets
cards.body: A CSS comment starts with /* and ends with */ and is ignored by the browser — use it to document code or temporarily disable a rule. A page can use all three style types together; the browser merges them, and for each property the highest-priority rule wins.

quiz.question: An external sheet sets 'p { color: red; }' and a <style> block placed AFTER the <link> sets 'p { color: blue; }'. What color is the paragraph?
quiz.explanation: Both rules have equal weight, so the later one (the internal style) wins and the paragraph is blue.

modules.title: CSS Selectors
modules.description: Choosing exactly which HTML elements a rule applies to — from universal and tag selectors to sub and attribute selectors.

cards.title: Universal & Tag Selectors
cards.body: The universal selector (*) matches every element on the page and is often used to reset spacing, e.g. '* { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }'. A tag (element) selector matches all elements with that name: 'p { color: red; }' styles every paragraph and 'h1 { color: blue; }' every level-1 heading.

cards.title: Group Selector
cards.body: Selectors that share the same declarations can be combined with commas: 'h1, h2, h3, p { color: red; font-size: 30px; }'. This avoids repeating the same block for every tag, keeps the style sheet short, and means a single edit updates all of the grouped elements.

quiz.question: Which symbol separates the selectors in a group selector?
quiz.explanation: A comma lets one declaration block apply to several selectors, e.g. 'h1, h2, p { ... }'.

cards.title: ID Selector
cards.body:
An ID selector starts with a hash and targets one unique element: '#header { color: red; }' styles

. An ID must be unique within the page, must begin with a letter, cannot contain spaces, and may include letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.

cards.title: Class Selector
cards.body: A class selector starts with a dot ('.red { color: #FF0000; }') and can be reused on many elements, even of different tags. An element-specific class such as 'p.red' applies only to paragraphs with that class. An element can carry several classes separated by spaces, e.g. class='red look'.

quiz.question: Which selector targets every element that has class='menu'?
quiz.explanation: A class selector begins with a dot, so '.menu' matches all elements carrying the class 'menu'.

cards.title: Descendant & Child Selectors
cards.body:
A descendant selector (a space) matches elements nested at any depth: 'div p' styles every

inside a

. A child selector (>) matches only direct children: 'div > p' skips paragraphs wrapped inside another element such as an inner
or
.

cards.title: Adjacent & Sibling Selectors
cards.body: The adjacent sibling selector (+) matches the element that comes immediately after another: 'h1 + p' styles only the first paragraph right after each <h1>. The general sibling selector (~) matches all following siblings at the same level: 'h1 ~ p' styles every later paragraph.

quiz.question: What does the selector 'div > p' select?
options:
Only

elements that are direct children of a
quiz.explanation: The child combinator (>) restricts the match to direct children; a plain space would match any depth of nesting.

cards.title: Selecting by Attribute
cards.body: An attribute selector styles elements based on their attributes. '[title]' matches any element that has a title attribute, and 'div[id]' narrows that to divs that have an id. It works with any attribute and needs no extra class or ID to be added to the HTML.

cards.title: Attribute with a Value
cards.body: '[attribute="value"]' matches an exact value: 'input[type="text"] { border: 1px solid blue; }' styles only text boxes, and 'div[id="data"] { color: red; }' picks the div whose id is exactly 'data'. Put the value in quotes and remember it must match the complete value.

quiz.question: Which rule styles only <input type='email'> fields?
quiz.explanation: Square brackets select by attribute, and [type='email'] matches only inputs whose type is exactly 'email'.

modules.title: Background, Text & Font Properties
modules.description: Colors, images, text formatting and fonts that give a page its look.

cards.title: Color & Image
cards.body: 'background-color' accepts a color name, a hex value (#F0E68C) or rgb(240,230,140). 'background-image: url(image/peek.jpg)' adds a picture, which repeats in both directions by default. Always set a fallback background-color in case the image fails to load.

cards.title: Repeat, Position, Size & Shorthand
cards.body: 'background-repeat' (repeat, repeat-x, repeat-y, no-repeat) controls tiling, 'background-position' places the image, 'background-attachment: fixed' keeps it still while scrolling, and 'background-size: cover' fills the box. The 'background' shorthand sets many of these at once; 'background-origin' and 'background-clip' control where the image starts and where it is painted.

quiz.question: Which 'background-size' value scales the image so it completely covers the element?
quiz.explanation: 'cover' enlarges the image until the whole box is covered (cropping if needed), while 'contain' fits the whole image inside the box.

cards.title: Text Formatting
cards.body: 'color' sets text color, 'text-align' (left, right, center, justify) aligns it, 'text-decoration' adds underline, overline or line-through, and 'text-transform' changes case (uppercase, lowercase, capitalize). 'text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px gray' adds a shadow defined by horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius and color.

cards.title: Spacing & Block Properties
cards.body: 'letter-spacing' and 'word-spacing' adjust gaps between characters and words, 'line-height' sets the distance between lines, and 'text-indent' indents the first line. 'vertical-align' aligns inline content, 'white-space: nowrap' stops wrapping, 'word-wrap: break-word' breaks long words, and 'text-overflow: ellipsis' shows '...' for clipped text.

quiz.question: Which property indents only the first line of a paragraph?
quiz.explanation: 'text-indent' pushes just the first line of a block inward; positive values indent and negative values pull it outward.

cards.title: Family, Size & Weight
cards.body: 'font-family' lists fonts in priority order, e.g. Arial, 'Times New Roman', serif — multi-word names need quotes, and a generic family comes last as a fallback. 'font-size' accepts px, em, % or keywords (the browser default is 16px = 1em). 'font-weight' uses normal, bold or the numbers 100-900.

cards.title: Style, Variant & Shorthand
cards.body: 'font-style' sets normal, italic or oblique; 'font-variant: small-caps' renders small capitals; 'font-stretch' makes a face condensed or expanded when the font supports it. The 'font' shorthand — 'font: italic bold 20px/1.5 serif' — follows the order style, variant, weight, size/line-height, family, and requires at least size and family.

quiz.question: Which two values are required in the 'font' shorthand?
quiz.explanation: The 'font' shorthand is only valid when it includes both a font-size and a font-family.

modules.title: Box, Border & Outline
modules.description: How the space around and inside every element is calculated, and how to frame it.

cards.title: The Box Model
cards.body: Every element is a box made of content, padding, border and margin, working outward. By default the total width equals left margin + left border + left padding + width + right padding + right border + right margin, and height is calculated the same way. 'width' and 'height' set the content size in px, cm, % or auto.

cards.title: Margin, Padding & box-sizing
cards.body: Margin is outer space and padding is inner space; each has -top, -right, -bottom and -left forms plus a shorthand taking 1 to 4 values (4 values = top, right, bottom, left). A fixed-width block is centered with 'margin: 0 auto'. 'box-sizing: border-box' makes padding and border count inside the declared width and height.

quiz.question: In 'margin: 10px 20px 30px 40px', in what order are the sides applied?
quiz.explanation: Four-value shorthand always runs clockwise starting at the top: top, right, bottom, left.

cards.title: Style, Width & Color
cards.body: 'border-style' accepts none, hidden, dotted, dashed, solid, double, groove, ridge, inset or outset; 'border-width' accepts thin, medium, thick or a length; 'border-color' accepts any color. The shorthand sets all three: 'border: 10px solid blue;'. A border only appears when a style other than none is set.

cards.title: Individual Sides
cards.body: Each side has its own properties — 'border-top', 'border-right', 'border-bottom' and 'border-left' — each with -style, -width and -color forms. 'p { border-left: 10px solid red; }' draws only a left border. Multi-value forms such as 'border-style: dotted solid double dashed' set top, right, bottom and left in that order.

quiz.question: Why might 'border: 5px red;' show no border at all?
options: No border-style is given, so it defaults to none
Borders also need a padding value
Red is not a valid border color
5px is too thin to be displayed
quiz.explanation: The default border-style is none; without a style such as solid, the width and color have no visible effect.

lessons.title: Rounded Corners, Border Image, Outline & Cursor

cards.title: Border Radius & Border Image
cards.body: 'border-radius: 30px' rounds every corner; up to four values set top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left (use 50% on a square element for a circle). 'border-image' slices a picture into nine sections and uses it as the border, e.g. 'border-image: url(border.png) 10 round;'.

cards.title: Outline & Cursor
cards.body: An outline is drawn outside the border and takes up no layout space: 'outline: 3px solid red;', with 'outline-offset' adding a gap. 'cursor' changes the mouse pointer — pointer for links, text for selectable text, not-allowed for disabled actions, wait for busy states, and resize cursors such as ns-resize.

quiz.question: How is an outline different from a border?
options: It is drawn outside the border and takes no layout space
It increases the element's total width
quiz.explanation: Outlines are painted outside the border box without affecting layout, unlike borders, which add to the element's size.

modules.title: Lists, Tables & Navigation
modules.description: Styling lists, data tables, links, navigation menus and image galleries.

cards.title: List Marker Properties
cards.body: Unordered lists use bullets and ordered lists use numbers or letters. 'list-style-type' sets the marker (disc, circle, square, decimal, lower-roman, upper-alpha and more), 'list-style-image: url(book.png)' uses a picture, and 'list-style-position' places the marker inside or outside the text block.

cards.title: Shorthand & Removing Bullets
cards.body: The 'list-style' shorthand combines type, position and image, e.g. 'ul { list-style: square inside; }'. 'list-style: none' removes the markers entirely and, together with 'margin: 0; padding: 0;', is the first step in turning a plain list into a navigation menu.

quiz.question: Which declaration removes the bullets from a list?
quiz.explanation: 'list-style: none' (or 'list-style-type: none') removes the list markers.

cards.title: Borders & Spacing
cards.body: Style a table with 'table, th, td { border: 2px solid blue; }'. 'border-collapse: collapse' merges neighbouring borders into one; with the default 'separate', 'border-spacing: 5px 10px' sets the gap between cells. 'caption-side' puts the caption at the top or bottom, and 'empty-cells: hide' hides empty cells (separate mode only).

cards.title: Size, Padding & Color
cards.body: 'width' and 'height' size the table or its th cells, and 'table-layout: fixed' makes column widths follow the first row for faster, predictable rendering. Padding on th and td adds breathing room, 'text-align' aligns content, and 'tr:nth-child(even)' with a background-color creates readable zebra stripes.

quiz.question: Which property merges adjacent table borders into a single line?
quiz.explanation: 'border-collapse: collapse' merges the borders of neighbouring cells; 'border-spacing' only works in the separate mode.

cards.title: Link States
cards.body: Links have four states styled with pseudo-classes: a:link (unvisited), a:visited, a:hover (mouse over) and a:active (while being clicked). Order matters — write them as link, visited, hover, active (LVHA) — so that later states can override earlier ones.

cards.title: Building a Navigation Menu
cards.body: Start with a <ul> of links inside <nav>, then 'ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }'. For a horizontal bar use 'li { display: inline-block; }', floats or flexbox, and give each link 'display: block; padding: 10px 20px;' so the whole area is clickable. Add 'a:hover { background: #333; }' for feedback.

quiz.question: In what order should the link pseudo-classes be written?
quiz.explanation: a:hover must come after a:link and a:visited, and a:active must come after a:hover, giving LVHA.

cards.body: Wrap each and its caption in a

cards.title: Image Sprites
cards.body: An image sprite combines many small images (such as icons) into a single file. Give an element a fixed width and height, set 'background: url(sprite.png)', and shift it with 'background-position: -40px 0' to reveal just one icon. Fewer image files mean fewer HTTP requests and faster page loads.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of using an image sprite?
options: It reduces the number of HTTP requests
It removes the need for CSS
quiz.explanation: One combined image replaces many small downloads, so the page loads faster.

modules.title: Layout: Div, Span, Display & Positioning
modules.description: Grouping elements and controlling how they flow, stack, float and align on the page.

cards.title: div and span
cards.body: is a block-level container that starts on a new line and takes the full width; use it to group sections of a page and style them together. is an inline container that sits within a line of text — ideal for styling a few words, e.g. 'This is important'.

cards.title: The display Property
cards.body: 'display: block' starts a new line and accepts width/height; 'inline' flows within text and ignores width/height; 'inline-block' flows inline but accepts width/height; 'none' removes the element from the layout. 'visibility: hidden' hides an element but keeps its space. Other values include flex, inline-flex, table, table-cell and list-item.

quiz.question: What is the difference between 'display: none' and 'visibility: hidden'?
options: hidden removes the element; none keeps its space
none removes the element from the layout; hidden keeps its space
quiz.explanation: A 'display: none' element takes up no space at all, while a 'visibility: hidden' element is invisible but still occupies its original space.

cards.title: static, relative, fixed & absolute
cards.body: The offset properties top, right, bottom and left work only when 'position' is not static. static (default) follows the normal flow; relative shifts an element from its normal spot; fixed pins it to the viewport so it stays put while scrolling; absolute positions it against the nearest positioned ancestor (or the page if there is none).

cards.title: z-index & Overflow
cards.body: 'z-index' sets the stacking order of positioned elements — the higher number appears on top. 'overflow' controls content that is bigger than its box: visible (default), hidden, scroll or auto, with 'overflow-x' and 'overflow-y' for each axis. It needs a block element with a limited height or width.

quiz.question: Against what is a 'position: absolute' element positioned?
quiz.explanation: An absolute element is placed relative to the closest ancestor that has a position other than static, falling back to the page if none exists.

cards.title: Float & Clear
cards.body: 'float: left' or 'float: right' pushes an element to the side so text and inline content wrap around it — classic for images in articles. 'clear: left | right | both' stops an element from sitting beside earlier floats and drops it below them. A container with 'overflow: auto' can enclose its floated children.

cards.title: Alignment & Dimension
cards.body: Centre text with 'text-align: center'; centre a fixed-width block with 'margin: 0 auto'; shift inline content with 'vertical-align'; or use flexbox for full alignment control. Dimension properties — width, height, min-width, max-width, min-height, max-height — keep elements within sensible limits as the screen size changes.

quiz.question: Which property stops an element from sitting next to a preceding floated element?
quiz.explanation: 'clear' moves an element below earlier floats on the chosen side(s), preventing it from wrapping alongside them.

modules.title: Flexbox
modules.description: A one-dimensional layout mode for building flexible, responsive rows and columns.

cards.title: Why Flexbox & display: flex
cards.body: Flexbox is a CSS3 layout mode that arranges items in a row or column, shares out spare space and aligns them without floats — making responsive pages much easier to build. 'display: flex' on a parent turns its direct children into flex items; 'inline-flex' does the same but keeps the container inline.

cards.title: Direction, Wrap & Alignment
cards.body: 'flex-direction' (row, row-reverse, column, column-reverse) sets the main axis; 'flex-wrap' (nowrap, wrap, wrap-reverse) allows multiple lines; 'flex-flow' combines both. 'justify-content' aligns items along the main axis (flex-start, center, space-between, space-around), 'align-items' along the cross axis, and 'align-content' aligns multiple lines.

quiz.question: Which property distributes flex items along the main axis (e.g. 'space-between')?
quiz.explanation: 'justify-content' controls main-axis distribution, while 'align-items' works on the cross axis.

cards.title: order & align-self
cards.body: 'order' changes an item's visual position without editing the HTML (default 0; lower numbers come first). 'align-self' overrides the container's align-items for a single item (auto, center, flex-start, flex-end, stretch, baseline) — handy for making one item sit at the bottom while the others stay centered.

cards.title: flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis & flex
cards.body: 'flex-grow' sets how much an item expands to take spare space (default 0), 'flex-shrink' how much it shrinks when space runs short (default 1), and 'flex-basis' its starting size (default auto). The 'flex' shorthand combines them, e.g. 'flex: 1 1 200px'. Giving every item 'flex: 1' makes them equal in width.

quiz.question: What does 'flex: 1' on every item in a row typically do?
options: Makes the items share the available space equally
quiz.explanation: 'flex: 1' lets every item grow equally into the free space, giving equal-width items.

modules.title: CSS Advanced
modules.description: Pseudo-classes, advanced attribute selectors, transitions, transforms and responsive design.

cards.title: Pseudo-classes
cards.body: A pseudo-class styles an element in a special state, written 'selector:pseudo-class'. Common ones are :hover, :active, :focus, :checked, :link and :visited, plus structural ones such as :first-child, :last-child, :nth-child(n), :first-of-type and :last-of-type — e.g. 'li:nth-child(odd) { background: #eee; }'.

cards.title: Pseudo-elements
cards.body: Pseudo-elements use double colons to style a part of an element. '::before' and '::after' insert generated content through the 'content' property ('p::before { content: 'Note: '; }'); '::first-letter' and '::first-line' style the start of text; '::selection' styles text the user highlights.

quiz.question: Which property is required for '::before' or '::after' to display anything?
quiz.explanation: Generated content only appears when the 'content' property is set, even if it is an empty string.

cards.title: Word, Prefix & Hyphen Matches
cards.body: '[class~="game"]' matches when 'game' is one whole word in a space-separated list. '[class|="game"]' matches exactly 'game' or values starting with 'game-' (such as game-super). '[class^="game"]' matches any value that begins with 'game', whole word or not, so 'gamesuper' matches but 'supergame' does not.

cards.title: Suffix & Substring Matches
cards.body: '[class$="game"]' matches values ending in 'game' (supergame, super-game), and '[class*="ga"]' matches values containing 'ga' anywhere. Together with ^= these power practical rules such as 'a[href$=".pdf"]' for PDF links and 'a[href^="https"]' for secure links.

quiz.question: Which selector matches class values that END with 'game'?
quiz.explanation: The $= operator matches the end of an attribute value, ^= the beginning, and *= any position.

cards.title: Transitions
cards.body: A transition animates a property change over time. A duration is essential — the default of 0s means nothing animates: 'div { transition: width 2s ease 0.5s; }'. Its parts are transition-property, -duration, -timing-function (ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, cubic-bezier) and -delay.

cards.title: 2D & 3D Transforms
cards.body: 'transform' moves, rotates, scales and skews elements: translate(x, y), rotate(45deg), scale(1.5), skew(20deg) and matrix(). 3D adds translateZ, rotateX/Y/Z and perspective(). 'transform-origin' changes the pivot point, 'perspective' and 'transform-style: preserve-3d' control depth, and 'backface-visibility: hidden' hides an element's reverse side.

quiz.question: A transition has no visible effect. What is the most likely missing piece?
quiz.explanation: Without a duration (default 0s) the change is instant, so no animation is visible.

cards.title: Media Queries
cards.body: A media query applies CSS only when conditions are met: '@media screen and (max-width: 768px) { body { background: lightgreen; } }'. Combine conditions with 'and', list alternatives with a comma (or), and negate with 'not'. Features include width, height, orientation and aspect-ratio.

cards.title: Columns & Filters
cards.body: 'column-count', 'column-width' and 'columns' split content into newspaper-style columns, with 'column-gap' and 'column-rule' (e.g. '5px solid red') styling the gap and divider, and 'column-span: all' stretching a heading across. 'filter' adds visual effects to images: blur(), brightness(), contrast(), grayscale(), hue-rotate(), invert(), opacity(), saturate() and drop-shadow().

quiz.question: Which rule applies styles only when the viewport is 768px wide or narrower?
quiz.explanation: max-width matches viewports up to the given width, while min-width matches viewports from that width upward.

units.title: Module 4: Bootstrap
units.description: Bootstrap setup and structure, the responsive grid, built-in UI components, utility classes and customization with CSS.

modules.title: Setup, Structure & Grid System
modules.description: Adding Bootstrap to a page and building responsive layouts with the 12-column grid.

cards.title: What is Bootstrap?
cards.body: Bootstrap is a popular front-end CSS framework used to create responsive, mobile-friendly websites quickly. It ships ready-made CSS classes and UI components (buttons, navbars, cards, forms, alerts), a 12-column responsive grid, and optional JavaScript for interactive parts such as dropdowns, modals and the collapsing navbar.

cards.title: Why Use Bootstrap?
cards.body: It saves time (no need to write all CSS from scratch), gives a consistent look across browsers, is mobile-first by design, and has huge community support and documentation. It is ideal for prototypes, dashboards, admin panels and business websites.

cards.title: Adding Bootstrap with a CDN
cards.body: A CDN loads Bootstrap's CSS/JS from an external server, so there is nothing to download. Add this inside <head>: <link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css" rel="stylesheet">

cards.title: Bootstrap JS & Local Files
cards.body: Add the JS bundle just before </body> for interactive parts like the navbar toggle: <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"></script>. You can also download Bootstrap and link it locally: <link href="bootstrap.min.css" rel="stylesheet">.

cards.title: CDN vs Download
cards.body: A CDN is quick to set up but needs an internet connection. Downloaded local files work offline and give you full control. Either way, the CSS goes in <head> and the JS goes at the end of <body>.

cards.title: Starter Template: Head
cards.body: <!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="UTF-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>My Page</title><link href="bootstrap.min.css" rel="stylesheet"></head>

cards.title: Starter Template: Body
cards.body: Hello, Bootstrap!

cards.title: Why the Viewport Tag Matters
cards.body: The viewport meta tag <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> is essential. Without it, mobile browsers will not scale the layout responsively.

quiz.question: Where is the Bootstrap CSS file generally included in an HTML page?
quiz.explanation: Bootstrap CSS is linked inside <head> so styles load before the page renders; the JS bundle usually goes at the end of <body>.

cards.title: Container → Row → Column
cards.body:
Bootstrap layouts follow the pattern Container → Row → Column:
Content
. The container sets the layout width, rows group columns horizontally, and columns hold the actual content.

cards.title: Container Types
cards.body: Use .container for a fixed-width, centered layout whose max-width changes at each breakpoint, and .container-fluid for a full-width layout across all screens. Responsive containers such as .container-md are full-width until the md breakpoint, then become fixed-width.

cards.title: Equal & Auto-Width Columns
cards.body: Plain .col classes divide the row equally: three .col elements each take one third. Using .col-auto makes a column only as wide as its content, and the remaining .col elements share the leftover space.

cards.title: Gutters (Spacing Between Columns)
cards.body: Gutters are the gaps between columns. Control them on the row with .g-* (both directions), .gx-* (horizontal) and .gy-* (vertical), e.g. <div class="row g-3">. Use .g-0 to remove gutters completely.

quiz.question: Which class creates a full-width container that spans the entire screen?
quiz.explanation: .container-fluid spans 100% of the viewport width, whereas .container has a fixed max-width at each breakpoint.

cards.title: The 12-Column Grid
cards.body: Bootstrap uses a 12-column grid. A row can contain up to 12 grid units, and each column can occupy a different number of units: col-6 is half the row, col-4 is one third, col-3 is a quarter. If the total in a row exceeds 12, the extra columns wrap onto a new line.

cards.title: Breakpoints
cards.body: Responsive classes apply different layouts to different screen sizes. The breakpoints are: sm (≥576px), md (≥768px), lg (≥992px), xl (≥1200px) and xxl (≥1400px). Classes without a breakpoint, like col-6, apply to all screen sizes.

cards.title: Mobile-First Behaviour
cards.body: Bootstrap is mobile-first: a class such as col-md-6 applies from the md breakpoint and up, and below it the columns stack vertically at full width. Example: <div class="col-12 col-md-6 col-lg-4"> is full width on phones, half width on tablets and one third on desktops.

cards.title: Offset, Order & Alignment
cards.body: Use .offset-md-2 to push a column to the right by 2 units, .order-1 / .order-2 to change visual order, and .justify-content-center or .align-items-center on the row to align columns horizontally or vertically.

quiz.question: What does <div class="col-12 col-md-6"> do?
options: Full width on small screens, half width from md upward
Half width on phones, full width on desktops
Always half width on every screen
Hides the column on md screens
quiz.explanation: col-12 applies by default (full width, stacked), and col-md-6 takes over from the md breakpoint upward (half width).

modules.title: Buttons, Navbar & UI Components
modules.description: Using Bootstrap's ready-made components to build common interface elements.

cards.title: Button Classes
cards.body: Bootstrap provides predefined button styles using the .btn class plus a style class: .btn-primary (primary action), .btn-secondary (secondary action), .btn-success, .btn-danger, .btn-warning, .btn-info, and .btn-light / .btn-dark. Example: <button class="btn btn-primary">Save</button>.

cards.title: Outline Buttons & Sizes
cards.body: Use .btn-outline-* (e.g. .btn-outline-danger) for outlined buttons with a transparent background and a coloured border. Change the size with .btn-lg (large) or .btn-sm (small).

cards.title: Button States & Block Buttons
cards.body: Add .active for the pressed look and the disabled attribute (or .disabled on links) to disable a button. For a full-width button, wrap it in <div class="d-grid"> so the button stretches across its container.

cards.title: Using .btn on Different Elements
cards.body: The .btn class works on

quiz.question: Which class creates an outlined red button?
quiz.explanation: Outline styles use .btn-outline-* with a colour name; danger is Bootstrap's red, so .btn .btn-outline-danger.

cards.title: Navbar Components
cards.body: A navbar is used to create website navigation using the .navbar component. .navbar-brand is the website or brand name, .navbar-nav is the container for navigation links, .nav-item is an individual navigation item and .nav-link is the link itself.

cards.title: Responsive Navbar
cards.body: Navbars can be made responsive: .navbar-expand-lg keeps links in a row on large screens and collapses them behind a toggle (hamburger) button on smaller ones. This needs a .navbar-toggler button, a .collapse.navbar-collapse wrapper and the Bootstrap JS bundle.

cards.title: Colours & Positioning
cards.body: Style a navbar with colour classes like .navbar-dark .bg-dark or .navbar-light .bg-light. Position it with .fixed-top (stays at the top), .fixed-bottom, or .sticky-top (sticks while scrolling). Align items using utilities like .ms-auto to push links to the right.

cards.title: Navbar Example
cards.body:
MySite
  • Home
  • About

quiz.question: Which class is used for an individual navigation link in a Bootstrap navbar?
quiz.explanation: .nav-link styles each link; .nav-item wraps it, .navbar-nav wraps the list and .navbar-brand is the site name.

cards.title: Cards
cards.body:
A card groups related content in a flexible box:
Title

Text

Go
. Cards combine well with the grid to build product or blog listings.

cards.title: Alerts
cards.body: Alerts show contextual feedback messages: .alert with .alert-success, .alert-danger, .alert-warning or .alert-info. Add .alert-dismissible with a .btn-close button (and the JS bundle) to let users close the message.

cards.title: Badges & Other Components
cards.body: A badge (.badge .bg-primary) is a small label for counts or status. Bootstrap also includes modals, dropdowns, accordions, carousels, tooltips and progress bars, which are activated with data-bs-* attributes.

quiz.question: Which class shows a red error-style message box?
quiz.explanation: .alert-danger gives the alert a red 'danger' theme, used for errors and critical messages.

cards.title: Form Controls
cards.body: Use .form-control on text inputs, email fields and <textarea> elements for full-width, consistently styled controls. Use .form-label for labels, .form-select for dropdowns, and .form-check with .form-check-input / .form-check-label for checkboxes and radio buttons.

cards.title: Layout & Input Groups
cards.body: Combine forms with the grid (.row and .col-*) to place fields side by side. An .input-group lets you attach text or buttons to an input, e.g. an @ symbol before a username or a Search button after a search box.

cards.title: Validation Styles
cards.body: Bootstrap provides .is-valid and .is-invalid for field states, with .valid-feedback and .invalid-feedback for the messages. Combine them with HTML attributes like required to give users clear feedback.

quiz.question: Which class styles a text input in a Bootstrap form?
quiz.explanation: .form-control gives inputs and textareas Bootstrap's full-width, consistent styling.

modules.title: Utility Classes
modules.description: Small predefined classes for spacing, text, colours, borders and display.

cards.title: Margin & Padding
cards.body:
Utility classes are small predefined classes used to apply common styling quickly. m-* is margin and p-* is padding. Side-specific versions: mt-* (top), mb-* (bottom), ms-* (start/left) and me-* (end/right); mx-* / my-* set both horizontal or both vertical sides. Example:
Content
.

cards.title: The Spacing Scale
cards.body: Values run from 0 to 5: 0 = no space, 1 = 0.25rem, 2 = 0.5rem, 3 = 1rem, 4 = 1.5rem, 5 = 3rem. Use mx-auto on a block element with a set width to centre it horizontally. Negative margins and responsive spacing like p-md-4 are also available.

cards.title: Width, Height & Gap
